stopbang.title: STOP-Bang Risk Index for Obstructive Sleep Apnea

preface.definition:
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) [ 26 ] is the most prevalent sleep-breathing disturbance, 
                                affecting about 34% of men and 17% of women.
                                A sleep apnea episode is a cessation of breathing (apnea) or 
                                a marked reduction in airflow (hypopnea) during sleep.
                                An episode is considered clinically relevant if it lasts more than 10 seconds; 
                                episodes of apneas and hypopneas often persist for 30-60 seconds.
                                It is estimated that the average life span of someone with untreated OSA is 58 years.

acb.title: Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB)
acb.root_preface:
Many medications can induce "brain fog,"
                                an additional layer of impairment that may mask actual cognitive decline.
                                In particular, the additive effects of anticholinergic medications, 
                                known as their Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB),
                                have been well studied. [ 4-7 ] The total ACB score evaluates the degree of impairment induced by someone's
                                current medications.
                                Each medication is scored from 0 to 3, and these scores are summed.
                                The criteria for these "0 to 3" values are:

Termed a possible anticholinergic.

headers: Potential alternatives offering a lower ACB Score

postface.text:
The total ACB score is 7 . This cognitive burden adds a layer of masking atop any existing
                                cognitive decline, making it difficult to determine someone's actual status.    Notes: Each definite anticholinergic,
                                of which there are currently 2 ,
                                may increase the risk of cognitive impairment
                                by 46% over 6 years. For each one-point increase in the total ACB score, 
                                a decline in someone's Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score
                                of 0.33 points over 2 years has been suggested. 
                                
                                Thus, the current anticholinergic burden may be lowering an MMSE score by 2 points.

leqembi.heading: Assessing Eligibility for Leqembi
leqembi.legend_preface:
A genetic analysis, amyloid positivity, and a brain MRI scan are required 
    to be eligible for these treatments,
    after first satisfying a number of initial criteria, shown below. [ 29 ]
preface:
Leqembi (generic name: lecanemab )
    is a prescription medication designed to treat Alzheimer's disease (AD).
    It is a monoclonal antibody that can
    reduce buildup of aggregated forms of amyloid beta, 
    which is frequently seen in the brains of those with AD.
    Leqembi
    is likely to be most effective in early stages of cognitive decline, 
    that is,
    for those diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) 
    or 
    mild Alzheimer's disease.
    It is administered via a series of monthly intravenous (IV) infusions.

lifestyleRecommendation.title: Lifestyle Recommendations
lifestyleRecommendation.preface:
The recommendations below tailor those published in the FINGER study.
                In a notable cover story,Scientific Americansummarized the study results:
                “A gold-standard clinical trial provides evidence that diet, exercise and
                an active social life can help prevent cognitive decline.”[20]

recommendations.details:
Include walks, music, meditation, naps, yoga, qigong, 
or whatever provides relaxation, at least once each day.
Avoid highly stress-inducing behaviors, such as 
staying up all night,
red-eye or international flights, 
unceasingly-stressful jobs, or 
staying in chronically-bad relationships.
The importance of a positive attitude cannot be overstated.
recommendations.comments:
People who are often stressed are more likely 
to experience brain shrinkage and increased production of the amyloid beta peptide.
Some stresses are unavoidable, 
but low stress levels are important for delaying or avoiding symptom onset.

recommendations.details:
Bedtime, 
rather than wake time,
makes a big difference.
Bedtime before midnight is preferable.
recommendations.comments:
Seek treatment for
Obstructive sleep apnea, which can cause poor sleep quality.  This medication may be disrupting sleep: donepezil. Is an alternative appropriate?

recommendations.details:
Fast every night for at least 12 hours, 
between the last food in the evening and the first in the morning.
Begin the fasting at least 3 hours before bedtime.
recommendations.comments:
Memory loss is observed in people producing too much amyloid beta peptide, 
which oligomerizes readily and can induce toxicity.
A key mechanism for clearing amyloid beta isautophagy.  
Nightly fasts (and an occasional daytime fast) can 
inhibit the mTOR pathway, 
induce autophagy, and 
clean up amyloid beta, 
damaged mitochondria (via mitophagy), and 
damaged or insoluble proteins.

recommendations.details:
Physical exercise has an anti-aging effect on the hippocampus region of the brain.
Exercise at a moderate activity level 4 to 5 times each week, 
for 30 to 60 minutes each time.
Heart rate should be raised 
(but not so much as to create too much stress, 
induce vascular problems, 
or damage joints).
Include both cardiovascular exercise and 
resistance training (weight-bearing or weight-lifting strength exercises).
Losing more than 10% of muscle mass disrupts function of the immune system.
recommendations.comments:
Effective exercise to enhance neuroplasticity includes a vigorous aerobic component 
(such as dancing or brisk walking) and
alternates with resistance training.
Studies also show that novelty is helpful.  
For example, 
it is better to be playing during exercise than simply doing a treadmill.  
Novelty can be introduced through 
games, 
play with family members or friends, 
or activities with pets.

Your genes indicate that you are part of the 12% of the population
for whom any exercise should work for weight loss.

recommendations.details:
Find ways to push mental abilities: 
become a tutor,
learn a new language, 
take dance lessons & dance often,
learn to play a musical instrument,
memorize poems,
even do math problems mentally.
Read books (rather than short articles).

Good social activities include bridge & chess,
and walking & talking with friends.
recommendations.comments:
Do crossword puzzles or Sudoku;
computerized crossword puzzles have been shown to slow cognitive decline.[21]Participate in activities like these 4 or more times a week, 
for at least 30 minutes each time.
These all support the promotion of neuronal connections.
